problem: DRL-based goal-oriented semantic policies for ObjectNav struggle to retain long-term object semantic information and lack goal-oriented ability, forcing extensive exploration and inefficient navigation.
motivation: Efficient object-goal navigation in unfamiliar environments requires the policy to exploit semantic structure and relate global and local information to the goal. Hand-designed feature extractors limit this, so self-attention is proposed to learn goal-relevant features automatically.
key_idea: Replace hand-designed feature extraction in the DRL semantic policy with multi-head self-attention (MHSA) so the policy learns goal-relevant semantic features and global-local correlations.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The abstract claims that multiple attention heads attend to different semantic features and capture global-local correlation, which improves accuracy and generalization across goals and environments.
method: MHSA-based goal-oriented semantic policy: uses multi-headed self-attention to extract features relevant to the goal from semantic input, replacing manual feature extractor design
Multiple attention heads: attend simultaneously to different semantic features to extract key information about the target goal
SemGO model: object-goal navigation model built on this policy, handling intricate semantic structures and linking global and local information

setting.backbone: MHSA-based DRL policy (SemGO), trained with deep reinforcement learning
setting.training_data: not stated in abstract; evaluated on the Gibson dataset
